develop-test-transfer.title: Our mission
develop-test-transfer.description: IRESEN connects research with Morocco’s energy transition and sustainable development needs. Together with its partners, it helps inform decisions, advance solutions and strengthen capabilities by bringing together people, expertise and resources.

figures.title: IRESEN in figures
figures.description: 69 collaborative projects supported, +60 patents filed, +1000 young researchers supported, +1100 scientific publications and +18 university laboratories established.

research-priorities.title: Research themes serving the energy transition
research-priorities.description: Produce reliable renewable energy and integrate it into electricity systems through durability, storage, active grids and demand flexibility. Develop renewable hydrogen and derived molecule value chains by connecting production, water resources, logistics and relevant industrial uses. Reduce industrial energy demand and process emissions through heat recovery, electrification and performance measurement. Connect water, energy and agriculture needs to preserve resources and strengthen system resilience. Recover value from residual resources and extend equipment life, considering available feedstocks, competing uses and environmental balances. Preserve comfort and essential services with less energy through solutions adapted to buildings, territories and climatic conditions. Adapt low-carbon transport to usage patterns, grid constraints and climate through fleets, charging, batteries and logistics.

HomeInnovation.searchText: Innovation value chain: national needs, anticipation, ideation, research, development and innovation (R&D&I) programming, support, scaling up, experimentation, demonstration, maturation, valorisation, technology transfer, adoption and impact assessment. Within Research & Innovation, develop, test and valorise connect needs with uses, with feedback between the work. An adaptable pathway: each project follows the stages relevant to its needs.
HomeInnovation.label: Landmarks in the research and innovation pathway

choose-pathway.label: Your need

items.title: Inform a decision
items.description: Explore a question through knowledge, data and technological options. Describe the context, the choices to prepare and the people or organisations concerned.

items.title: Advance a solution
items.description: Connect a research question with scientific work, testing or experimentation. Explain what already exists and which uncertainties remain.

items.title: Strengthen capabilities
items.description: Share methods and know-how, learning through research and practice. Identify the audiences, the skills needed and the intended applications.

items.title: Prepare a result for use
items.description: Explore maturation, valorisation or transfer within Research & Innovation. Describe the result, its stage and the uses being considered.

choose-pathway.note: These entry points complement one another. The expertise, facilities and partners to involve depend on the need, available capabilities and the collaboration framework.

items.title: Businesses and industry
items.description: Bring a practical problem, process constraints, shareable data and an experimentation setting. Joint work helps clarify options and implementation conditions.

items.title: Research teams
items.description: Bring a scientific question, methods and expertise. Define the work, experimental resources and ways to document results together.

items.title: Institutions and territories
items.description: Share a decision-making need, local characteristics and the actors concerned. Connect analysis and research with local application conditions.

items.title: Partners and funders
items.description: Connect teams and contribute resources, knowledge or cooperation. Clarify roles, shared objectives and each partner’s contribution.

collaboration-arrangements.label: The framework

items.title: Collaborative research
items.description: Connect scientific objectives, partner contributions, resources, expected results and monitoring arrangements within a project or programme.

items.title: Expertise and shared facilities
items.description: Examine analysis, testing, experimentation or training needs and the conditions for mobilising skills and infrastructure.

items.title: Networks and exchanges
items.description: Connect actors through partnerships, networks, institutional exchanges and events. The World Power-to-X Summit and IRSEC’X illustrate these approaches according to their objectives.

collaboration-arrangements.note: Scope, responsibilities, resources, timing, access conditions and arrangements for sharing results need to be defined before work begins.

need-to-project.label: Building together

items.title: Clarify the need
items.description: Identify the problem, users or beneficiaries, application context and the decision or result sought.

items.title: Examine contributions
items.description: Consider useful expertise, data, facilities and partners. Identify uncertainties, constraints and availability to confirm.

items.title: Define the work
items.description: Set objectives, tasks, deliverables, resources and monitoring criteria, distinguishing expected results from effects to measure.

items.title: Formalise and learn
items.description: Clarify the collaboration framework, then document the work, use of results and lessons to share.

need-to-project.note: These pointers are not an admission procedure. A call for projects or a specific scheme retains its own conditions.

collaboration-references.label: Examples

items.title: Mapping
items.description: An example of decision support: mapping the country’s renewable resources and zoning to inform energy choices.

items.title: WorldPtX Summit
items.description: An example of connection and exchange around Power-to-X. An event is a means of cooperation; its results should be documented against its objectives.

collaboration-references.note: Read a reference alongside its need, partner roles and stage. It does not establish that an equivalent arrangement is available for every new request.

prepare-discussion.label: First discussion
prepare-discussion.note: Start with a non-confidential summary. Arrangements for sharing sensitive documents and carrying out the work are clarified later with the relevant teams.
checklist: Your organisation, your role and partners already involved.
The problem, the people concerned and the intended application.
Work completed, available results and remaining uncertainties.
The expertise, facilities or forms of cooperation you are seeking.
Timing, field conditions, data and resource constraints to discuss.

results-to-transfer.label: The results

items.title: Knowledge and methods
items.description: Scientific results, protocols and methods can be shared, reused or adapted to advance other work.

items.title: Technologies and prototypes
items.description: Equipment, a process or a prototype opens up possible uses. Its performance, limitations and actual stage need to be explained.

items.title: Skills and know-how
items.description: Lessons from research and experimentation can strengthen practice, training and team capabilities.

items.title: Data and decision tools
items.description: Analysis, datasets and tools can inform choices. Their scope, use conditions and limitations matter as much as their dissemination.

results-to-transfer.note: Begin by identifying what was produced, by whom, for which need and with what evidence.

research-to-use.label: Maturation

items.title: Establish the result’s stage
items.description: Describe its origin, the need addressed, contributions and available evidence. Distinguish what is demonstrated from what still needs checking.

items.title: Test the conditions
items.description: Examine performance, constraints and limitations in relevant conditions. Testing may lead back to further research.

items.title: Prepare for use
items.description: Identify users, necessary adaptations, resources and partners. Clarify technical and organisational conditions for use.

items.title: Document and learn
items.description: Follow use where it exists, qualify observed contributions and share lessons for future work.

research-to-use.note: Maturation is not automatic progression. A result can contribute to research, a decision or training without leading to commercial transfer.

transfer-pathways.label: Possible pathways

items.title: Share knowledge
items.description: Publications, learning resources, methods and scientific exchanges make lessons accessible through suitable dissemination arrangements.

items.title: Co-develop with partners
items.description: Continue work with actors involved in use to adapt, qualify or test a solution and clarify respective contributions.

items.title: Prepare technology transfer
items.description: Examine access or licensing arrangements where the result, rights and partners allow. Conditions still need to be established.

items.title: Explore an entrepreneurial initiative
items.description: Consider creating or developing an activity around a result where the team, need and maturation conditions are suitable.

transfer-pathways.note: No pathway is guaranteed by a prototype, publication or patent filing. Choices depend on evidence, rights, capabilities and the partners involved.

intellectual-property.label: The conditions

items.title: Which result and contributions?
items.description: Describe the origins of knowledge, data and work, the partners involved and material already shared. Contributions should be clearly attributable.

items.title: Which rights and uses should be examined?
items.description: Clarify existing rights, intended uses, sharing conditions and responsibilities to discuss. The applicable framework is defined with the relevant teams; this page does not provide a standard contract.

items.title: How should a first discussion be prepared?
items.description: Begin with a non-confidential description of the result and need. Before sharing sensitive material, clarify confidentiality arrangements and useful documents with the relevant contact.

intellectual-property.note: A patent application, a granted right and an active right are distinct situations. None alone establishes transfer or adoption.

adoption-initiatives.label: Concrete examples

items.title: iSmart
items.description: An electric-vehicle charging station presented among IRESEN’s achievements. To examine its valorisation, distinguish the product, contributions and uses actually documented.

items.title: AquaSolar
items.description: A mobile, modular desalination unit powered by solar energy. The demonstrator illustrates an application; its presentation alone does not establish commercial transfer.

adoption-initiatives.note: Evidence of use or impact should specify the actors, context, stage, period and observed results. Intentions remain distinct from measured effects.

build-transfer.label: Your result
build-transfer.note: The first discussion addresses the result, the need and conditions to examine. It is neither a funding commitment nor a transfer agreement.
checklist: The result or technology, its origin and contributing actors.
The need, potential users and application context.
Existing work, testing and evidence, including known limitations.
The maturity stage and adaptations or checks still needed.
Partners, rights and constraints to discuss, without sharing confidential material.
